one_line: This ad explains facial asymmetry using mirror vs. photo comparisons to pitch Refina AI for previewing cosmetic changes.

hook.what_happens: A woman's face is shown with the text 'You've never seen your own face.'
hook.why_it_works: It uses a counterintuitive psychological hook that immediately grabs attention.

shots.description: Portrait of a woman's face flipping horizontally to show mirror vs. photo versions.
Stacked split screen comparing mirror view and camera view.
Portrait with a yellow per-pixel difference heatmap overlay.
Portrait showing left-half doubled vs. right-half doubled faces.
Three-panel comparison of a second subject's face halves.
Portrait emphasizing natural asymmetry with text overlays.
Phone mockup demonstrating how to flip a photo in the camera roll.
Minimalist CTA screen with an interactive search bar typing 'Refina AI'.

devices.what_it_is: A vertical line wiping across the screen to reveal different image states.
devices.used_for: Comparing mirror vs. photo and left vs. right face halves.

devices.name: per-pixel difference overlay
devices.what_it_is: A yellow heatmap showing pixel variance.

devices.name: search bar UI
devices.used_for: Guiding the viewer to search for the product.

transcript.text: One of these is her photograph. The other is the same file, flipped. You have never seen your own face. A mirror reverses you. A photograph does not. So the face you know best is the one nobody else sees. Lay the photograph over its own mirror. This is every pixel where the two disagree. Two pictures of one face. One. Her halves are two different faces. Left side, doubled. Right side, doubled. Nothing added. Nothing drawn. Neither one is her. Two. Another face. The same operation. Two people again. It isn't her. It's everyone. Three. You have been practising in a mirror. Every expression you have ever checked, you checked reversed. The photograph is the version you have seen least. None of this means your face is wrong. The asymmetry is the part that is actually yours. You just watched two faces lose it. So test it. Open your camera roll. Find a photo of yourself and flip it. That is who everyone has been looking at. If you are about to change something on that face, see it on yours first. Not on a stranger's. A preview, not a promise. Search Refina AI.

narrative_arc: Introduce the concept that we don't know our own true faces.
Explain the difference between mirror images and photographic reality.
Demonstrate facial asymmetry visually using pixel overlays and doubled halves.
Explain the psychological impact of practicing expressions in a reversed mirror.
Reassure the viewer that asymmetry is natural and unique.
Provide an interactive, immediate action step for the viewer to try.
Introduce Refina AI as the solution to previewing cosmetic changes on your true face.

cta.what: Search 'Refina AI' to preview cosmetic changes on your actual face.

subjects: Subject 1: Young woman with brown hair in a bun (primary model).
Subject 2: Older woman with greyish-blonde hair (secondary model).
what_makes_it_work: An engaging, mind-bending hook about self-perception.
Highly scientific and clean visual demonstrations of asymmetry.
An immediate, low-friction interactive task ('Try it now') that drives user engagement.
Directly addresses a common anxiety in cosmetic procedures (unnatural previews).

animations.what_moves: Left and right halves of the face portrait
animations.purpose: Shows how doubling one side of the face creates two distinct people.
animations.reusable_as: Splitting a single product into its component halves.

animations.reusable_as: Displaying a team roster or product lineup.

animations.purpose: Introduces the interactive app interface for the call to action.
animations.reusable_as: Showcasing mobile app features or screenshots.

animations.name: Interactive Swipe Flip
animations.what_moves: A cursor hand and the image inside the phone frame
animations.purpose: Demonstrates the user interaction required to flip the photo.

animations.what_moves: Text characters inside a search input field
animations.purpose: Directs the user on what to search for to find the app.
animations.reusable_as: Simulating search queries or command-line inputs.
animations.would_need_building: Text typing effect with a blinking cursor.

animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements scale up with elastic overshoots or fade in with staggered timing.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements fade out in place or are wiped away by transition lines.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts synchronized with sweeping wipe lines that reveal new states.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The central alignment of the subject's face remains locked to emphasize asymmetry.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Deliberate and educational, pausing on static comparisons before executing quick, clean transitions.

what_we_should_steal: Asymmetry Heatmap Scan for high-tech data visualization overlays.
Symmetrical Face Convergence for engaging split-screen comparisons.
Search Bar Typing for clear, actionable call-to-action sequences.
